title: Basic Linear Regression — Flashcards
description: Twenty source-grounded recall cards for Chapter 2.

cards.front: What does Pearson correlation r measure?
cards.back: The strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is the range of any Pearson correlation coefficient?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: Why can y=x^2 have r=0?
cards.back: Correlation measures linear relationship only; the symmetric quadratic relationship is perfect but nonlinear.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What correlation did SALES and POP have in the Wisconsin Lottery sample?
cards.back: r = 0.886, indicating a strong positive linear relationship.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: The least-squares slope is b1 = r times ______ divided by ______.
cards.back: s_y; s_x.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: The least-squares intercept is b0 = ______ minus b1 times xbar.
cards.back: ybar.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is a fitted value yhat_i?
cards.back: The regression-line estimate b0+b1x_i for response y_i.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is a residual e_i?
cards.back: The observed response minus its fitted value: y_i-yhat_i.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: State the least-squares variability decomposition.
cards.back: Total SS = Error SS + Regression SS.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What does R-squared measure?
cards.back: The proportion of response variability explained by the regression line.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is MSE in basic linear regression?
cards.back: s^2 = Error SS/(n-2), the unbiased estimator of sigma^2.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What are the error degrees of freedom in basic linear regression?
cards.back: n-2, because two coefficients determine the line.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What three conditions reduce se(b1)?
cards.back: More observations, smaller residual standard deviation s, and greater spread s_x in the explanatory variable.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What null hypothesis tests whether the explanatory variable is important?
cards.back: H0: beta1=0.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is the 95% confidence interval formula for beta1?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is a prediction interval designed to cover?
cards.back: A new individual response at x*, not merely the mean response.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is heteroscedasticity?
cards.back: Variability that changes by observation rather than remaining common.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What is a high leverage point?
cards.back: An observation unusual in the horizontal, x-direction.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What CAPM slope classification does the text give for b1>1?
cards.back: Aggressive; slopes below one are defensive.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex

cards.front: What compact matrix form represents basic linear regression?
cards.back: y = X beta + epsilon.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_013 - 2 Basic Linear Regression.tex
